text:
Ridly Greig's season has been about a new job. Back from injury on Nov. 10, he's taken on more of the shutdown role (NHL.com asked this week whether he's become a shutdown specialist), and with William Eklund out, his ice time has climbed to about 18 minutes a night. Ottawa has won three straight and is 4-0-1 in five with him in the lineup.

The scoring hasn't followed. He has five points in 18 games, 0.95 per 60, under the bottom of our talent range, and no power-play points. Part of that is luck that should turn (shooting 9.7% against a range around 12%), and the Senators have scored 8.0 goals more than expected with him on the ice anyway, which says the line is fine. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season is worth keeping in mind: he played with very strong teammates, and his results ran well ahead of his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net (82nd percentile for home-plate chances) and exiting cleanly 62% of the time. He's had five shots in each of his last two games.
